chapter.title: When it goes wrong: loops, made-up facts, and wrong turns

cards.body:
The agent reported the file was sent. No tool ever sent it.

Picture your intern at 5pm saying *all done!* while the envelope is still sitting on their desk. **Agents go wrong in 3 ways you can actually see**, and each one leaves a different mark in the *log*, the step-by-step record of what the agent thought and did.
cards.simpler: The agent said the file was sent. But no tool ever sent it. Think of an intern at 5pm saying "all done!" while the envelope still sits on their desk. **Agents go wrong in 3 ways you can actually see**. Each one leaves a different mark in the log. The log is the step-by-step record of what the agent thought and what it did.

cards.prompt: You asked your intern to post 3 letters before lunch. They come back beaming: "All posted!" Which clue tells you what really happened?

options.text: How confident and cheerful they sound
The post office receipt, which lists 2 letters

whyNot.a: That's the report, not the record: an intern, or an agent, can sound just as sure about a letter that's still in their bag.
whyNot.c: That's a hint, not proof: 40 minutes fits 2 letters or 3. Only the receipt settles it.

cards.reteach: What someone says they did and what actually happened are two separate things. The post office wrote the receipt, not the intern, so it can't be wishful thinking. In an agent's log, the tool results play the part of the receipts.

cards.title: Claims and receipts
cards.body:
An agent's log has two kinds of lines. *Claims* are what the model says: "I'll search now", "Done!". *Receipts* are what a tool actually sent back: a file name, an error, zero results. **Trust the receipts, not the claims.**

Failure one is the *loop*: the same tool, with the same input, gets the same result, over and over. Think of an intern redialling a busy number for an hour.

Failure two is the *made-up result*: the model says something happened, but no receipt shows it. The model is built to write the most likely next sentence. After "attach the file", the most likely next word is "Sent!"
cards.simpler: An agent's log has two kinds of lines. Claims are what the model says, like "Done!" Receipts are what a tool sent back, like an error or zero results. **Trust the receipts, not the claims.** Failure one is the loop: the same tool, same input, same result, over and over, like redialling a busy number. Failure two is the made-up result: a claim with no receipt. The model writes the likeliest next words. After "attach the file," that's "Sent!"

cards.title: The email that never left
cards.body:
Goal: email the Q3 report to Priya. Step 1, the model thinks: find the file. Step 2, receipt: search_files found q3_report.pdf. Step 3, the model thinks: attach and send. Step 4, final answer: "Sent to Priya! Let me know if she has questions."

Now scroll through the whole log. **There is no send_email line anywhere.** Priya's inbox is empty, and the agent is already offering to answer her questions.
cards.simpler: The goal: email the Q3 report to Priya. First, the model thinks: find the file. Then a receipt: search_files found q3_report.pdf. Next, the model thinks: attach and send. Last, it answers: "Sent to Priya! Let me know if she has questions." Now read the whole log, top to bottom. **There is no send_email line anywhere.** Priya's inbox is empty, and the agent is already offering to answer her questions.

cards.prompt: Your agent is hunting for flights to Lisbon. Steps 4 to 19 all read: search_flights("Lisbon, Friday") → 0 results. Sixteen times, same words, same answer. What's going on?

options.text: Nothing's wrong, it's just being thorough

whyNot.b: That's the made-up result, not the loop: every step here has a real receipt behind it. The receipts just keep saying 0.
whyNot.c: That's being thorough mixed up with being stuck: a thorough agent would try something new, like another day or airport. The same input with the same 0, sixteen times, is a loop.

cards.reteach: You spot a loop by the repeats: the same tool line, same input, same result, again and again. Nothing new goes in, so nothing new comes out. Like an intern redialling a busy number, it won't stop by itself.

cards.title: The quiet one
cards.body:
You'd think the loud failures are the scary ones. The quiet one is worse. Failure three is the *wrong turn*: every receipt is real, nothing repeats, and the agent neatly solves a problem you never asked it to solve.

You ask for the cheapest flight to Portland, meaning Maine. The agent books Portland, Oregon, on the other side of the country, and the log looks spotless. It's the intern who stays late tidying the wrong filing cabinet perfectly.

To spot it, **put the goal at the top of the log next to what the tools actually touched**. If they name different things, the agent took a wrong turn.
cards.simpler: The quiet failure is worse than the loud ones. Failure three is the wrong turn: every receipt is real, nothing repeats, and the agent neatly solves a problem you never asked about. You ask for the cheapest flight to Portland, meaning Maine. It books Portland, Oregon, across the country, and the log looks perfect. **Put the goal at the top of the log next to what the tools actually touched.** If they name different things, it took a wrong turn.

cards.body: Sam's agent finishes with "Done! 3 invoices paid." Sam reads that last line, closes the laptop, and goes home. If they'd scrolled up, they'd have found just one pay_invoice receipt. The other two payments were only claims. **For every claim in the final answer, find the receipt that backs it up**, and count.
cards.simpler: Sam's agent ends with "Done! 3 invoices paid." Sam reads that last line, shuts the laptop, and goes home. If they had scrolled up, they would have seen only one pay_invoice receipt. The other two payments were just claims. **For every claim in the final answer, find the receipt that backs it up**, and count them.

cards.prompt: Goal: "Rename my Rome trip photos by date." The log shows 48 real rename receipts, none repeated, every one in the folder Holiday/Paris. Which check catches the problem?

options.text: Look for the same line repeated
Find a receipt behind each claim
Compare the goal with what the tools touched

whyNot.a: That's the loop check, not this one: all 48 renames hit different files, so nothing repeats.
whyNot.b: That's the made-up-result check: here every claim has a real receipt. The receipts just point at Paris.

cards.reteach: A wrong turn hides inside a clean log. The only way to see it is to put the goal next to the receipts: the goal says Rome, the receipts say Paris. The work is real, but the target is wrong.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body:
An agent goes wrong in 3 ways you can see in its log: it repeats the same step, it claims something no tool did, or it neatly solves the wrong problem. **Trust the receipts, not the final message**, and check the goal against what the tools actually touched.

Tomorrow: how a web page your agent reads can quietly give it orders.
cards.simpler: An agent can go wrong in 3 ways you can see in its log. It repeats the same step. It says something happened that no tool did. Or it neatly solves the wrong problem. **Trust the receipts, not the final message.** Then check the goal against what the tools actually touched. Tomorrow: how a web page your agent reads can quietly give it orders.

cards.body: Turn on web search in a chatbot and ask it for a fact with a number in it. Open the source it links to and find that number on the page. If it isn't there, you've just caught a made-up result.
cards.simpler: Turn on web search in a chatbot. Ask it for a fact that has a number in it. Then open the source it links to and look for that number on the page. **If the number isn't there, you've just caught a made-up result.**

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now read an agent's log, point to the step where it went wrong, and say whether it was a loop, a made-up result, or a wrong turn.
